title: Deprecating a zod-inferred theme token: Omit + re-add with @deprecated JSDoc
answers: How do I mark a theme token as deprecated so TypeScript shows a strikethrough/warning?
Why is there an Omit<..., 'field'> & { field: string } pattern in createComponents.ts?
zod schema .describe() isn't making editors warn about deprecated usage
body:
Symptom: a theme.components.* field needs a @deprecated TSDoc tag so editors warn consumers, but it's typed via z.infer from a zod schema and zod's .describe() string doesn't surface as a TS @deprecated hint.
Root cause: ThemeComponents in createComponents.ts is derived with DeepRequired<z.infer<...>>, which only carries the zod .describe() text, not a @deprecated JSDoc comment.
Fix pattern: Omit the field from the zod-inferred type and re-add it manually with an explicit '/** @deprecated ... */' comment in the exported type (see ThemeTableColors = Omit<InferredThemeTableColors, 'rowSelected'> & { rowSelected: string }), while keeping the zod schema's .describe() text in sync as the runtime/JSON-schema description.
Constraints: use this only for fields you intend editors to flag as deprecated; for plain optional/required changes just edit the zod schema directly. Keep the zod .describe() wording and the TS @deprecated comment text identical (schema.generated.json description is generated from .describe()).
applies: Any theme.components.* (or similarly zod-schema-derived) token being deprecated in packages/grafana-data/src/themes.
